plan.summary: A2 gives the map a say in who can trade with whom. Today two nations can only sign a deal if they touch; after A2 goods can cross other people's ground, and the countries in between charge for the privilege — a standing agreement with a mode (road, rail, port), a volume cap, a rate, a term and a notice period, negotiated the same way a trade deal is. Each toll is charged on what actually arrives rather than what set out, so the country nearest the seller collects the most and every crossing after it is worth less; Canada and Mexico work as shortcuts at a flat ten per cent that nobody collects, and a Great Lakes port reaches the world only through Canada while an ocean port reaches it directly. A corridor holder can close a route with a year's notice, which costs them standing with the injured party and with everyone watching — the same machinery a later stage will use for walking out of a trade deal. Nothing about what a deal is worth changes: A2 only takes a bite out of the income on its way home, and the old one-click ways to sell abroad are left exactly as they are so no nation loses income while this is being built.
decisions: ONE MODULE, NOT TWO: js/transit.js holds both the corridor graph and the agreement register, rather than a separate js/routes.js — one reset, one save section, one script tag, and the graph and the permission check cannot drift apart.

THE TOLL LANDS IN A NEW WORLD PHASE, NOT INSIDE Deals.tick: Transit.tick runs between js/world.js:1221 and :1222 inside the same batch, so `git diff js/deals.js` shows only the new `route` field and the scope rule is provable by reading one diff.

PLAN AND SETTLEMENT ARE NET, DISPLAY IS NET, SETTLEMENT ITSELF IS UNTOUCHED: Deals.settlement stays gross and byte-identical; Transit.keep(d) multiplies it at the four places that report income. For every deal the game can sign today keep is exactly 1.0, so nothing moves.

plan.perTurn AND plan.gain ARE NET OF CARRIAGE, with a separate `Carriage` effects row — because the AI reads preview.gain (js/ai.js:318) and a routed deal valued at its face is the M11.1 defect reinstated; direct deals are unaffected because keep is exactly 1.

THE REACH GATE WIDENS IN plan BUT NOT IN legal: js/moves.js:482-484 becomes `adjacent OR routable`, while js/moves.js:1486's candidate loop keeps Game.adjacentNations — so the player can sign routed deals, the AI cannot propose them (that is A4), and tests/moves.test.js:389 never has to change.

HOP-LAYERED MAX-PRODUCT RELAXATION, NOT DIJKSTRA: a hop cap makes plain shortest-path answer 'no route' where a shorter permitted route exists, and multiplication is bit-identical across engines where Math.log is not.

MODE TIERS ARE HIGHWAY, RAIL, PORT — the brief's three — as grantable bits; OCEAN/LAKE/CANADA/MEXICO live in a separate node-attribute table, because four of them are properties of a place and not of a border.
AN INTERMEDIARY MUST PERMIT BOTH EDGES IT TOUCHES, each at the mode actually used to cross it — anything less reproduces the single-best-mode defect that retires js/panels.js:1098.

A NEW Relations KIND `revoked`, NOT REUSE OF `reneged`: rel.magReneged is -1.4 and is tuned for invading a nation you signed a pact with (written at js/moves.js:904), which is not what a noticed, lawful exit costs.

REVOCATION USES THE REAL WITNESS PATTERN: Moves.remember(grantor, [grantee], 'revoked', scale, tune) — victims get the kind, onlookers get 'witnessed' at -0.05 (js/moves.js:85-92) — rather than writing the full grievance into every neighbour.

THE CANADA/MEXICO CORRIDOR BYPASSES THE AGREEMENT MACHINERY ENTIRELY: no verdict, no negotiation, no grant record, no revocation, no credit to anybody — a corridor node is priced by a tunable and nothing else, which is the owner's ruling made structural rather than remembered.

ONE ASK IS ONE NEIGHBOUR: a route is built only from agreements that already exist. A re-route may never sign anything, because a deal quietly buying a corridor from a nation the player has never spoken to is worse than a deal that stops paying.

VOLUME CAP IS A HARD CUT, OLDEST CONTRACT FIRST: Transit.load returns the SET of deal ids that did not fit, not a running total — pro-rata means a stranger's new deal silently shrinks your income with no event to explain it.

THE OLD ONE-OFF EXTERNAL SALE AND ONE-OFF TRANSIT PAYOUT SURVIVE A2 UNCHANGED (js/actions.js:609-621, :639-679, and trade.cooldownTurns with them) — retiring them is A2b, because fourteen of sixty nations have no other income and a half-built replacement makes a quarter of the board unplayable.
NOTICE IS FOUR TURNS (transit.noticeTurns 4), matching the largest value in deal.countdownAt, so a player learns one warning rhythm for a deal running out and a route closing rather than two.
NODE ORDER IS A PLAIN STRING SORT of living nation ids, then '@canada', '@mexico', '@world' — correct for both id formats that exist, and needing no knowledge of either.

Step 6 changes the call to `capacityNote(T, res, tName)` and adds a test.

THE FIVE-HOP THRESHOLD IS NOT trade.worldMarketPenalty ALONE. A deal pays every turn (js/deals.js:136) while a world sale is one-off and gated by trade.cooldownTurns 3, so the crossover is worldMarketPenalty / (deal.rate x (cooldownTurns + 1)) = 0.45 / (0.25 x 4) = 0.45 at today's defaults — a coincidence js/tunables.js:674 already documents. All four tunables go in the guard test, or moving deal.rate to 0.5 makes a five-hop chain the best move in the game while the test stays green.

THE NEGOTIATED FLOOR BREAKS THE FIVE-HOP GUARANTEE ON ITS OWN. Five hops at the 0.05 floor keep 0.95^5 = 0.774 — comfortably profitable. Compounding alone does not price out a long route; that is why transit.hopFriction exists and why the ceiling test is written as an inequality over the tunables rather than against a hardcoded number.

A QUARTER OF THE BOARD HAS NO WORLD MARKET TO LOSE TO. docs/spec/a2-measurements.md measures 14 of 60 nations fully landlocked; js/actions.js:468 disables the world-market button on `acc.any`, so 0.45 is not their alternative. The guarantee is stated against the world market and the exception is written down rather than assumed away.

'A FIVE-HOP RESALE CHAIN IS UNPROFITABLE' CANNOT BE DELIVERED BY A2, AND THE 'IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION' ARGUMENT IS WRONG. VERIFIED: js/moves.js:356-357 computes freeB(i) = ts.surplus[i] - committed[i]; js/market.js:103-116 recomputes surplus LIVE every call; js/deals.js:118 books a buy as -vol fixed at signing. So once a buyer's own production drifts positive, freeB = positive - negative and it can offer on more than it produces. The clamp that would fix it is one line in js/moves.js:357 and it changes what an A1 deal can cover — A1's work or a new area, not A2's. A2 measures the routing form of the metric and the plan says so out loud.

PERFORMANCE FIGURES: use docs/spec/a2-measurements.md, which nobody cited — 256 bordering pairs, 2 ms to classify all of them, 735 Moves.plan calls per AI round at 0.208 ms each. js/world.js:56's 8.0 ms is the cost the columnar-buffer rewrite REMOVED, not a current phase cost, and must not be quoted as headroom. The measured ruling — build the graph once per turn, make the lookup cheap — is adopted verbatim.

MODE TIERS NEED A PORT BIT. The routing design's enum has none, yet the whole justification for retiring js/panels.js:1098 was that it cannot express 'grant highway, refuse port'. Step 3 defines PORT as a grantable tier and keeps OCEAN/LAKE/CANADA/MEXICO out of the grantable mask.

steps.step: Build the nation-level corridor graph, once per turn
steps.where: js/transit.js, private. Reads Game.graph(), Game.state().owner, Game.ownerEpoch(), Game.areaTransport (js/game.js:1292), the step-1 areaExport fields.
steps.detail: MODE = { HIGHWAY: 1, RAIL: 2, PORT: 4 } — the brief's three tiers, and the only bits a grant may carry. Node attributes (oceanPort, lakePort, canadaGateway, mexicoGateway) live in a SEPARATE table, because four of them are properties of a place, not of a border. NODES in a fixed order: living nation ids sorted as plain strings, then '@canada', '@mexico', '@world'. LAND EDGES: one sweep over the Area CSR graph; where owner[i] !== owner[nb] and both sides carry rail, the edge carries RAIL; both sides highway, HIGHWAY. An edge with neither mode does not exist for goods — that is js/panels.js:1113's null case promoted from a UI filter to a graph fact. CORRIDOR EDGES: nation <-> '@canada' if it holds a Canada gateway Area, or a lakePort Area (the lake edge requires MODE.PORT — the owner's ruling made an edge); <-> '@mexico' if it holds a Mexico gateway. SINK: nation -> '@world' if it holds an oceanPort Area (requires MODE.PORT); '@canada' and '@mexico' -> '@world' unconditionally; '@world' has no outgoing edges, so nothing can launder through it. Built ONCE PER TURN, keyed on (ownerEpoch, the held Graph identity, a module-local worldSeq bumped by reset). The worldSeq is not belt-and-braces: Game.reset() sets ownerEpoch back to 0 (js/game.js:264), so a cache on epoch alone serves the previous world's borders to a fresh world. docs/spec/a2-measurements.md measured the whole rebuild at 2 ms for 256 bordering pairs against 153 ms of AI planning; its ruling is the rule — the graph is built once per turn, the lookup is what runs per plan.
steps.greenAfter: 'the graph is a pure function of the board' — build twice with no turn advanced and deepEqual; move a county and assert it changed. 'no route across water' — every edge appears in Game.borderingNations, never only in Game.maritimeNations. 'a border with neither rail nor highway is not a border for goods'.

steps.step: The route search and the toll arithmetic, with the five-hop guard
steps.where: js/transit.js: `from(nid, opts)`, `find(a,b,opts)`, `toWorld(nid,opts)`, `priceRoute(route, volume, tune)`. New tunables in js/tunables.js group 'Trade'.
steps.detail: HOP-LAYERED MAX-PRODUCT RELAXATION. State is (node, hopsUsed, corridorsUsed); relax k = 1..transit.maxHops over a fixed sorted edge list. Not Dijkstra: a hop cap makes plain shortest-path report 'no route' where a shorter permitted route exists, and a layered sweep has no priority queue whose heap order could differ. NO Math.log — the textbook -ln(factor) sum is not specified bit-identical across engines and a replay that diverges because the player changed browser is the worst bug this project can produce; multiplication is IEEE-754 exact-rounded, and every factor is in (0,1] so the product is monotonically non-increasing. TIE-BREAK, a total order: higher keep, then fewer intermediaries, then the lexicographically earlier node-id sequence — never iteration order. Note in the comment that 'simple paths for free' rests on that tie-break and not on the factors, because transit.tollMin, transit.hopFriction and transit.foreignCorridorToll all have a minimum of 0. priceRoute IS THE ONE SPELLING OF THE ARITHMETIC, a loop and not `V * product`: `carried = V; for each intermediary: if corridor, carried *= (1 - foreignCorridorToll); else take = carried * rate, carried = (carried - take) * (1 - hopFriction)`. A route with no intermediaries never enters the loop, so keep is exactly 1.0. Returns { keep, delivered, legs:[{node, kind, mode, rate, take}] } so whoever applies the cost never re-derives it. THE STRATEGIC POINT, and it belongs in the comment: each toll is charged on what arrives, so the nation nearest the seller collects the most and every hop after it is worth less.
steps.greenAfter: 'tolls compound rather than add' (0.2 and 0.2 delivers 0.64 before friction, not 0.60). 'the nation nearest the seller collects the most' (legs[0].take > legs[1].take at equal rates). 'the most generous route in the game still loses to the alternative' — a tunables-only test over transit.tollMin, transit.hopFriction, transit.foreignCorridorToll, transit.maxHops, transit.maxCorridors, trade.worldMarketPenalty, deal.rate and trade.cooldownTurns, no world booted. 'the hop cap does not hide a shorter route'. 'the same world gives the same route twice, and again after reset and rebuild'.

steps.step: The agreement register, and permissions asked at relax time
steps.where: js/transit.js: the record, live/get/permits/forNation/grant/tick; the `allow(node, mode)` predicate inside the search.
steps.detail: RECORD: `{ id:'t7', grantor, grantee, mode, cap, rate, since, duration, notice, status:'live'|'noticed'|'ended', noticedTurn, noticedBy, endsTurn, endedTurn, reason }`. Keyed on the DIRECTED triple (grantor, grantee, mode) — Nevada carrying Idaho's goods is a different object from Idaho carrying Nevada's, and mode-separated because the brief requires a state to grant highway and refuse port. `rate` is fixed at signing exactly as a deal's price is; carriage reads the rate stored on the hop, never the grant's current rate, so a grantor cannot re-price under a running contract. permits() checks BOTH status and TERM — `if (rec.since + rec.duration - turn < 1) return null` — mirroring js/deals.js:290-291, so a D-turn grant carries exactly D turns whichever side of Deals.tick it is ticked on. A 'noticed' grant still permits while `turn < endsTurn`: that is what a notice period means. THE CORRIDOR BRANCH COMES FIRST AND SHORT-CIRCUITS EVERYTHING: grantor '@canada' or '@mexico' returns `{rate: transit.foreignCorridorToll, transfer: false, grantId: null, cap: null}` always — no agreement, no opinion, no revocation, nobody credited. PERMISSIONS ARE NOT BAKED INTO THE GRAPH: an intermediary u on (v,u,w) requires allow(u, mode(v,u)) AND allow(u, mode(u,w)), each edge checked against the mode actually used and recorded per leg. Baking grants into the graph would invalidate a per-turn rebuild on every signature; asking at relax time is why the rebuild stays rare. Ids are 't'+seq from a serialized counter (offers 'x'+offerSeq — single character, so the copied `Number(id.slice(1))` sort cannot produce NaN). tick() walks grants in ascending numeric id and does four things: drop grants whose grantor or grantee no longer exists (the Pacts rule), close 'noticed' grants at endsTurn, expire by term, prune ended records past nation.historyWindow.
steps.greenAfter: 'a grant is per mode and per direction' — grant highway A->B, then permits(A,B,'rail'), permits(A,B,'port') and permits(B,A,'highway') are all null. 'grant highway, refuse port' — goods route THROUGH successfully and to '@world' not at all. 'a grant carries for exactly its term'. 'you cannot revoke Canada, and Transit.live('@canada', anyone, anyMode) is null'. 'an agreement round-trips exactly, ids included, and seq continues rather than restarting'.

steps.step: Revocation with notice, and the record F2 stands on
steps.where: js/transit.js serve(id, by, turn, tune) / withdraw(id); Moves.planRevoke/resolveRevoke; new kind in js/relations.js:71-88 and a magnitude in js/tunables.js.
steps.detail: serve() sets status 'noticed', noticedTurn, noticedBy, endsTurn = turn + rec.notice. EITHER SIDE MAY SERVE: a grantee walking away from a corridor it is paying for is the same instrument seen from the other end, and refusing it would make the grantee's only exit a breach. THE COST IS PAID WHEN NOTICE IS SERVED, not when it takes effect — it is a price for the decision, paying at effect would let a nation serve notice on the last turn of a game for free, and the injured party should see the entry the same turn they start counting down. WHAT IT COSTS: `Moves.remember(grantor, [grantee], 'revoked', 1, tune)` — the real witness helper at js/moves.js:85-92, so the grantee records 'revoked' and every other adjacent nation records 'witnessed' at rel.magWitnessed -0.05. A NEW KIND, not `reneged`: rel.magReneged is -1.4, is written only at js/moves.js:904 when you invade a nation you signed a pact with, and js/relations.js:133 clamps to [-1,1], so one entry at scale 1 would pin the injured party at the Hostile floor for a lawful exit. AND THE APPEND-ONLY RECORD, in the js/pacts.js:97/:180 shape: `notices.push({ turn, by, against, agreementId, mode, kind: 'transit' })`, decayed out at nation.historyWindow * 2, with `reneges(nid)` counting inside the window and `standing(nid) = grantsHeld - reneges * transit.renegeWeight` reusing the js/pacts.js:117-122 asymmetry — signing is cheap, so the number must be able to go negative or a serial revoker out-signs their own reputation. `kind` is present from day one with only one value, so F2 appends `kind:'deal'` with no schema change. Withdrawing a notice restores the route and does not unsay it: each notice writes its own memory, so notice-then-withdraw punishes itself. Giving notice does NOT use the turn, on the js/actions.js:391-398 precedent (no money, no ground, no army); what stops it being spammed is the reputation. NOTE FOR F2, written in the header: this stage gives F2 the reputation half and the notice-period pattern; F2 still has to add a notice field to js/deals.js, because A2 does not put one there.
steps.greenAfter: 'notice keeps the route running and paying for exactly transit.noticeTurns turns, then closes it' — the boundary, because off-by-one here is the difference between a threat and a formality. 'revocation is remembered by the injured party and by the neighbourhood, and it decays' — Relations.score falls, adjacent nations carry 'witnessed', reneges is 1, and after nation.historyWindow * 2 it is 0. 'the notice record carries a kind from the day it has only one value'. 'withdrawing restores the route and does not restore the reputation'.

steps.step: Put a route on a deal, take the toll in its own phase, and show it
steps.where: js/deals.js:171-191 (the sign record), :441-445 serialize, :447-460 loadState — AND NOTHING ELSE IN THAT FILE. New Transit.carriage/keep/netFor/tick. js/world.js between :1221 and :1222. js/moves.js:482-484 and :530-547. js/panels.js:1045, :1070; js/dealbook.js:66, :90.
steps.detail: THE DEAL GAINS ONE FIELD: `route: plan.route || null` — null means direct, keep exactly 1.0, and a pre-A2 document loads that way with no migration. serialize deep-copies it the way js/deals.js:443 already deep-copies `flows`; a shallow spread passes the round-trip test and still leaves the loaded game sharing hop objects with the live one. THE TOLL LANDS IN A NEW PHASE, not inside Deals.tick: `Transit.tick(tn, turn, {player})` runs immediately after js/world.js:1221 and before js/world.js:1222, inside the same batch, and for each live routed deal debits (1 - keep) x that turn's gross from the two parties and credits each transferring leg's grantor with Game.earn. js/deals.js's settlement and tick are not edited at all, which is what makes the scope rule provable by reading one diff. NO OVERDRAW IS POSSIBLE and it must be said, because Game.earn does not clamp (js/game.js:1626-1632): the debit is a share of the credit Deals.tick just made for that same deal, so it can never exceed it. CONSERVATION IS THE INVARIANT: sum(legs' takes) + delivered === gross exactly, and the corridor legs are the only leak, on purpose. RECOMPUTE THE ROUTE'S PRICE EVERY TICK from the stored hops; do not store a multiplier — a float in the save that could disagree in its last bit with the fold is a treasury drifting by cents over sixty turns with nothing to point at. THE FOUR DISPLAY SITES: js/panels.js:1045 and js/dealbook.js:66 multiply their per-deal figure by Transit.keep(d, tune, turn); js/panels.js:1070 and js/dealbook.js:90 call Transit.netFor(nid, tune, turn) instead of Deals.income. Both new readers default `turn` the way js/deals.js:150-151 does, or a two-argument caller reports zero for a noticed grant. THE REACH GATE: js/moves.js:482-484 becomes `adjacent OR Transit.reaches(nid, target, turn)` — the adjacency branch is untouched, so every pair the game can already sign passes exactly as before, including the maritime pairs tests/deals.test.js:29/:162/:181 walk. js/moves.js:1486's candidate loop is NOT touched, so the AI's view of the world does not move. plan.perTurn and plan.gain become net of carriage with a separate `Carriage` effects row; for a direct deal keep is exactly 1.0, so tests/deals.test.js:97-126 is byte-identical.
steps.greenAfter: 'a routed deal's gross settlement is exactly what it would have been with no route' — deepEqual(Deals.settlement(d, T()), the same flows with route nulled). 'the tolls plus what arrives equals what the deal pays' — sum every treasury before and after a tick and assert the total fell by exactly the corridor share and by nothing else. 'a neighbour is still a neighbour' — every currently-adjacent pair routes with zero intermediaries and keep exactly 1.0. 'routing leaves the price index byte-identical' for signing and for a whole term. 'a save carries no route data it did not need, and a routed deal round-trips with its hops deep-copied'.

steps.step: Volume caps, stalls, and the reason a player can act on
steps.where: js/transit.js load(turn) and the stall path; Transit.tick.
steps.detail: `load(turn)` walks EVERY live deal in ascending numeric deal id — the same order Deals.tick settles in, so the older contract has the prior claim on the corridor, which is what a contract means — accumulates each deal's full value against every hop's grant, and returns the SET of deal ids that did not fit. Not a running total compared per hop: a total that exceeds the cap would stall every deal on that hop including the oldest. Demand is the deal's FULL value on every hop, not the post-toll value arriving there: a corridor does not carry less tonnage because somebody upstream charged more, and using the arriving value would let one grantor's rate change another grantor's capacity. HARD CUT, NOT PRO-RATA: a stalled deal is a thing the player can act on and A3 can draw; a 7% haircut with no event to explain it is not. A STALLED DEAL IS STALLED, NOT VOIDED: it earns nothing this turn, `d.paid` is not incremented, and its TERM KEEPS RUNNING DOWN — so a corridor holder who revokes can burn a five-year deal to nothing, which is the drama the stage exists for. `route.stalled = {turn, at, why}` with why in 'revoked' | 'lost' | 'capped' | 'expired' — the exact record docs/spec/economy-system-spec-addendum-a.md's A3 needs for 'click a broken link to open negotiation with whoever now controls that hop'. On a stall, try ONE re-route from grants either party already holds (plus corridor hops, which need none) — and a re-route MAY NEVER SIGN ANYTHING, because a deal quietly buying a corridor from a nation the player has never spoken to is worse than a deal that stops paying. Re-routes are applied at the END of the tick, after the load snapshot has been used, so a re-routed deal cannot exceed a cap invisibly. LOGGING follows js/deals.js:264-268: one entry when a deal first stalls and one when it resumes, player only — sixty AI deals stalling every turn is 3,600 entries against a 4,000 cap. Failure reasons are ranked so the message is actionable: 'no-path', 'no-mode', 'too-far', 'no-permission' with blockedAt naming the first nation that has not granted.
steps.greenAfter: 'a corridor over its cap carries the older contract and stalls the newer', and the younger resumes when the older ends. 'a revoked corridor stops a running deal from paying, and the clock keeps running'. 'a re-route never signs anything' — Transit.count() unchanged. 'a route the graph cannot draw is refused, and it says who to talk to'. 'a dead corridor holder does not leave a ghost' — the route reports blockedAt rather than pricing a country that no longer exists.

steps.where: js/actions.js:556-635 renderTransitPreview rewritten; new showTransitCard() in js/panels.js after showRenegotiation (:172-257) plus a line in js/shell.js after :260 and a chain inside js/panels.js:251's handler; new Routes tab in js/dealbook.js:133-171.
steps.detail: THE ASK PANEL, top to bottom: three mode buttons in the existing `.dur-opts` row A1 built for the term (road / rail / through their port), each disabled with a title saying why not; a volume-cap row; the duration row using the same termWords() the deal panel uses; THE CHAIN — 'Your goods would cross Nevada, then Utah. You would keep 58% of what this deal pays', one line per hop with its rate, and Canada shown as a hop reading '10%, which nobody collects — the goods are simply worth less'; the corrected capacity note; the toll slider opening at trade.openingOfferFactor; a plain line saying who may end it and with how much notice; Propose. Every control re-plans and re-renders, and re-rendering clears #deal-response so a stale verdict can never sit under changed terms (js/actions.js:599). The panel renders plan fields and computes nothing (js/actions.js:681-689's rule). THE CARD: one showTransitCard switching on kind ('ask' | 'notice') exactly as showRenegotiation switches on 'new' | 'renew' at js/panels.js:206. An ask gets three `.crisis-opt` buttons — let them through at their number, counter at Moves.transitVerdict's ask (the same function that judges the player when the player asks, so they are shown the number the game would have demanded on their behalf), or no — answered on the spot against transit.askerFloor, because a multi-turn haggle is a card per round trip. A notice gets 'Look for another way through' and 'Understood'. The chain at js/panels.js:251 must be mirrored both ways or an answered deal card leaves a queued route card waiting a full round. THE ROUTES TAB in the Deals screen, second of three because it explains the first: 'Routes you use' (through whom, mode, what it costs you a quarter, turns left, a free 'Give it up' — dropping a route you use only hurts you) and 'Routes you grant' (to whom, mode, cap, what it pays you, turns left, 'Give notice' behind the two-step confirm shape proposeDeal already uses). AND THE ONE LINE THAT MAKES A2 LEGIBLE BEFORE A3 EXISTS: each Running row gains a sub-line reading '-18% - through Nevada and Canada' when the deal is routed, so the toll and the deal it comes off sit in the same row. Rewrite js/dealbook.js:15-19's header, which currently says the screen is read-only because deals run their term — true of deals, no longer true of routes.
steps.greenAfter: The full suite green, plus the telemetry counters (opened / proposed / signed / noticed) the alpha needs to answer 'does the threat of revocation land?' with a number rather than an impression.

tunables: transit.foreignCorridorToll — v 0.10, min 0, max 0.5, step 0.01, group 'Trade', label 'Canada / Mexico corridor toll'. doc: 'What a shipment loses passing through Canada or Mexico. Aaron's ruling of 5 September: flat, not negotiated, and a COST rather than a transfer — neither country is an actor here, neither has a treasury, and neither receives this money. The trade is simply worth ten per cent less. transit.hopFriction is deliberately NOT charged on top, because flat means flat, which makes a foreign corridor the cheapest hop on the board and a Canada or Mexico gateway worth holding. One toll for the whole crossing, not one per border county: the ruling is about what the deal is worth, not about where you cross.'

transit.hopFriction — v 0.18, min 0, max 0.6, step 0.01, group 'Trade', label 'Changing hands at a frontier'. doc: 'What a shipment loses crossing one more country's ground, on top of whatever that country charges. Nobody collects it and it cannot be negotiated away — the goods are unloaded and reloaded at the frontier. It exists because tolls alone cannot make a long route bad: a rate can be negotiated down to transit.rateMin, and 0.95 to the fourth power is 0.81, so four countries of friends would still deliver four fifths of a deal. This is the number that makes distance cost, and it is the one that has to satisfy the bound in tests/transit.test.js. The bound is keep < trade.worldMarketPenalty / (deal.rate x (trade.cooldownTurns + 1)) — a deal pays every turn and a world sale pays once, so all four of those move it. Raising transit.maxHops or transit.maxCorridors without raising this reopens the long chain.'

transit.maxHops — v 4, min 1, max 8, step 1, group 'Trade', label 'Longest route (countries in between)'. doc: 'How many other people's ground a shipment may cross. Four, because five crossings is the length the success metric on the board is written against, so a five-hop route is refused with a sentence rather than priced. This is a cost and legibility bound and NOT the balance lever — what makes long routes bad is transit.hopFriction — and a route the trade map cannot draw is a route the player cannot argue with.'

transit.maxCorridors — v 1, min 0, max 2, step 1, group 'Trade', label 'Foreign corridors per route'. doc: 'How many times one shipment may leave the continent and come back. One. The spec calls Canada and Mexico corridors for a bordering state, not a network to be chained, and this is load-bearing on the long-route bound: at two, the most generous four-country route keeps 0.49 and beats the alternative, so transit.hopFriction would have to rise to about 0.22 to hold the line. Set to 0 to measure what the foreign corridors are actually worth.'

transit.rateMin — v 0.05, min 0, max 0.5, step 0.01, group 'Trade', label 'Lowest toll an agreement may carry'. doc: 'The floor a transit rate may be negotiated down to. It was already the floor — the Math.max(0.05, ...) clamp at js/actions.js:541 — and it is lifted into the schema because the long-route guarantee is arithmetic ON it: the claim is that the most generous route the game can produce still loses, and that sentence is only checkable if the most generous toll is a named number.'

transit.rateMax — v 0.60, min 0.1, max 0.95, step 0.01, group 'Trade', label 'Highest toll an agreement may carry'. doc: 'The ceiling a transit rate may be pushed to, the other half of the clamp at js/actions.js:541. Above this a corridor holder is not charging a toll, it is refusing passage, and refusing is already something they can do.'

transit.durations — v [4, 8, 20, 40], kind 'array', group 'Trade', label 'Transit grant durations (turns)'. doc: 'The menu of terms a transit grant may be signed for. Deliberately longer than deal.durations: a corridor renegotiated every four quarters is admin, and the thing that makes a corridor interesting is that it outlives the deals running over it. A duration outside this list is refused rather than rounded, the same rule deal.durations follows.'

transit.defaultDuration — v 8, min 1, max 80, step 1, group 'Trade', label 'Default grant duration (turns)'. doc: 'The term a grant carries when none was named, and where the duration row opens. Must be a member of transit.durations. Twice the default deal term, so a corridor signed today outlives the first deal that uses it and the player meets revocation before they meet expiry.'

transit.defaultCap — v 6000, min 0, max 100000, step 500, group 'Trade', label 'Default corridor capacity ($M/turn)'. doc: 'How much deal value a grant will carry in a turn before the traffic beyond it stops moving. Same units and the same default as trade.capacityPerGateway, so a corridor is worth about what a border gateway is worth. There is deliberately no uncapped grant: a cap the player never has to think about is not a decision, and the alpha is asking whether holding a corridor feels powerful.'

transit.noticeTurns — v 4, min 0, max 20, step 1, group 'Trade', label 'Notice before a route closes (turns)'. doc: 'How long a corridor keeps running, and keeps paying its toll, after either side gives notice. The grant still carries during the notice, which is what a notice period means and is the same rule that pays a deal for the turn it is closing. Four because it is the largest value in deal.countdownAt, so a player learns ONE warning rhythm for a deal running out and a route closing rather than two. FUTURE-IDEAS F2 will reuse this field for walking out of a trade deal.'

transit.renegeWeight — v 2, min 0, max 10, step 0.5, group 'Trade', label 'Revocation weight against standing'. doc: 'How many grants held one revocation cancels out, for the standing number. Above 1 on purpose and for the reason the treaty version already gives: signing is cheap, so a number that could not go negative would let a serial revoker out-sign their own reputation. This is the number F2 will read when a trade deal is walked out of.'

transit.maxOpenAsks — v 2, min 1, max 10, step 1, group 'Trade', label 'Route requests waiting at once'. doc: 'The most unanswered requests for a corridor one nation may be holding. Separate from deal.maxOpenOffers, and deliberately: the two queues raise separate cards at the end of a round, so a shared cap would let a full trade inbox silently swallow a route request. Two rather than three because a route is a smaller decision than a five-year trade deal. A NOTICE is never capped — a notice the player is not told about is a route that vanishes.'

transit.askerFloor — v 0.5, min 0, max 1, step 0.05, group 'Trade', label 'When the asker walks away from a counter'. doc: 'A nation that asked for a corridor and was countered accepts if it still keeps at least this much of what the route pays it, and walks otherwise. One rule, answered on the spot, so a player who counters gets a yes or a no immediately rather than a card per round trip.'

rel.magRevoked — v -0.35, min -3, max 0, step 0.01, group 'Relations', label 'Memory: they closed a corridor we were using'. doc: 'Bigger than taking one Area from us (rel.magAnnexed -0.22) and far short of tearing up a pact (rel.magReneged -1.4): closing a corridor with notice is a hostile act you were entitled to take, while a pact is a promise you signed. Recorded when NOTICE is served rather than when the route closes, because the harm starts the moment the other side has to re-plan. Onlookers get the existing witnessed term instead of their own key, the same structure a conquest already uses. A placeholder — the addendum says toll and reputation numbers get schema values and stay there until playtesters have an opinion.'

AMENDED IN THE SAME COMMIT, NOT NEW: trade.cooldownTurns (js/tunables.js:599) still reads 'Turns before the same partner can be traded with again', which has been false since A1 — it governs external sales and the one-off transit sale only. Fix the doc. And trade.transitToll's doc gains a sentence saying tolls now compound along a route, so a reader setting it to 0.6 understands that three hops keeps 6.4%.

NOTE ON GROUP SIZE: this takes 'Trade' from 26 keys to 40, the largest group in the schema. That is a real cost to the tuning dashboard and it is the price of putting every number in one place. tests/tunables.test.js fails on a duplicate key, so transit.maxHops must be registered exactly once.
notBuilding: THE AI INITIATING TRANSIT. 'transit' is deliberately absent from Moves.legal, so no AI proposes a corridor and the pinned move-type list at tests/moves.test.js:389 never changes. The addendum puts this in A4, and adding one candidate per neighbour per mode would roughly double what the AI scores every turn on a board nobody has tuned.

ROUTED DEALS IN THE AI'S CANDIDATE LIST. js/moves.js:1486 keeps iterating Game.adjacentNations, so the AI's view of who it can trade with does not move at all in A2. The player can sign routed deals; the AI cannot propose them until A4 does it deliberately.

THE EXTERNAL-SALE REWRITE. The one-off world / Canada / Mexico sale (js/actions.js:639-679) and the one-off transit-to-market payout (js/actions.js:609-621) survive A2 exactly as they are, cooldown and all, so tests/trade.test.js:148-173 stays green untouched. Fourteen of sixty nations are fully landlocked and this is their only external income; retiring it before its replacement is finished makes a quarter of the board unplayable. See splitStage.

THE TRADE NETWORK MAP. A3, and it ships immediately after. What A2 owes it is built: `route.stalled = {turn, at, why}` with why in revoked / lost / capped / expired, and a `blockedAt` naming the first nation that has not granted, which is what A3's 'click a broken link to open negotiation with whoever now controls that hop' is built on.

BREAKING A TRADE DEAL EARLY. D171 stands. A2 builds the notice period, the reputation cost and the append-only notices list with `kind` already on it, so F2 appends `kind:'deal'` rather than inventing a second idea about what breaking a promise costs. Said plainly so nobody thinks it was delivered: F2 inherits the reputation half whole, and still has to add a notice field to js/deals.js itself.

NEGOTIATING A WHOLE MULTI-HOP ROUTE IN ONE GO. One ask is one neighbour. A route is assembled from agreements that already exist, and a re-route may never sign anything, because a deal quietly buying a corridor from a nation the player has never spoken to is the thing js/moves.js:578-590 forbids in the strongest terms in this codebase.

THE RESALE-CHAIN HOLE. js/moves.js:357 computes free surplus as live surplus minus a commitment fixed at signing, so a nation whose own production has drifted positive since it bought can offer on more than it produces. That is a real hole and it is A1's arithmetic, not A2's — the one-line clamp changes what a deal can cover. Flagged to the owner with the test that proves it; not fixed here.

PRO-RATA CAPACITY SHARING, RIVER CORRIDORS, CHOKE POINTS AND BANK PAIRS. data/county_trade.json carries 15 choke_point counties, 213 bank_pairs and four named river corridors; none of them are read by any routing code and the brief asks for mode tiers, multiplicative tolls, foreign corridors and revocation. Building on them is building ahead of the brief. One note: build/build_economy.py:105 already reads choke_point into the baked economy, so the flag is not inert and re-baking it would move supply.
GOODS PHYSICALLY MOVING. The addendum defers quantity transfer past the alpha. Every toll in A2 is a share of income, never a share of tonnage.
keyTests: 'trade capacity did not move' — a fixture of Game.tradeCapacity(nid).total AND the full Game.exportAccess(nid) object for every nation on the seeded opening board, recorded before step 1 and asserted equal after. This is what catches somebody redefining `port` while adding `oceanPort`, and it is the only thing standing between A2 and a silent rebalance of every standing deal's volume on the whole board. If it goes red, A2 has become an economy change.

'a routed deal's gross settlement is exactly what it would have been with no route' — deepEqual(Deals.settlement(d, T()), the settlement of the same flows with route nulled — and, separately, `git diff js/deals.js` showing only the `route` field in sign, serialize and loadState. If it goes red, the toll has moved inside A1's arithmetic instead of coming off its income, which is the one thing the whole stage was scoped not to do.

'the tolls plus what arrives equals what the deal pays' — sum every treasury before and after a tick in which a routed deal settles, and assert the total fell by exactly the corridor legs' share and by nothing else, with the domestic legs' credits accounting for the rest. This single sum catches every arithmetic error in the toll path at once: money minted by paying gross and crediting the grantor on top, money destroyed by double-charging, and Canada being quietly credited in violation of the ruling.
plan.splitStage: "YES — ONE PART, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE DESIGNS FEARED. The external-sale rewrite should be its own stage, A2b, shipped immediately after A2 and before A3. That means: retiring the one-off transit-to-market payout (js/actions.js:609-621), rewiring the world-market button onto standing agreements so a landlocked nation sells abroad through a corridor it holds rather than through a negotiation it re-opens every three turns, and putting the Great Lakes ruling on the player's screen — a lake port reaching the world only through Canada at the flat ten per cent, an ocean port reaching it directly, a river port reaching neither. Three reasons it is a stage and not a step. It is the only part of A2 that can leave a nation with no income at all: docs/spec/a2-measurements.md measures 14 of 60 nations fully landlocked and 2 more lake-only, and js/actions.js:468 gates their world-market button on exportAccess.any, so a half-landed replacement is a quarter of the board unable to earn. Its failure mode is invisible to the suite — nothing anywhere in tests/ asserts what the external path pays, so a wrong number surfaces in play rather than in a run. And it is the only part that changes a number that has already been tuned: today a Great Lakes nation sells at the full world rate and would newly lose ten per cent, and 59 of the 136 port counties are river ports that would newly reach nothing. A2 as ordered above is strictly additive — a new instrument, a new cost on a new kind of deal, nothing existing paying differently — and that is what makes it safe to build in one pass. A2b changes what existing nations already earn, and should be scoped, measured and argued on its own. THE COST OF SPLITTING, said plainly: for the length of A2 the game offers two ways to buy passage — the old one-shot toll on the trade panel and the new standing agreement — which is confusing, and alpha question 2 ('does holding a corridor feel powerful?') gets tested on routed deals only. Both are acceptable because the alpha does not run until after A4, and neither is worth the risk of the alternative. Everything else in A2 stays together: the graph, the search, the register, the verdict, revocation and the screens are one mechanism, and splitting them would ship a cost nobody can see or a screen with nothing behind it."
